column1: # Gaps of the 'server' block that are no longer gaps, keyed to the same
# 'killed' means a mutation taken from this sweep's output now fails a test.
# 'equivalent' means the mutation is real and the program is the same either way.
# 'superseded' means the line the verdict belongs to was replaced by a fix.

column6: why

ClientCookie.Length != 8 || ServerCookie[0] != Version, the second connective of the validator's guard chain. The version octet is inside the eight octets the keyed hash is computed over, so a cookie whose version is wrong has a MAC that cannot match - the explicit check decides nothing the comparison below does not decide again, and nobody without the secret can make the two disagree
the return false of HasValidServerCookie when no cookie secret is set. Its one caller opens with DNSCookieSecret is not null, so the method never runs in the state this line answers for

the CNAME-and-ANY guard of FollowCanonicalNames, which is called only where the store answered NoData - and a node holding a CNAME answers Found to a query for CNAME or for ANY. The guard is right, says why in its own comment, and cannot be reached
!TryStripTSIG(...) || unsigned is null - the second term cannot be true when the first is false
above = CompareCanonical(Name, owner) > 0, where Name is a name the zone does not hold and owner is one it does
unsigned is null || tsig is null, the same chain one term along
below = CompareCanonical(Name, next) < 0 - next is the next existing name, so the same argument

Request.HTTPMethod == POST, guarding the body read. The comment above it warns that asking a GET for its body would wait for octets never promised - and the constructor call below asks every request for Request.HTTPBody whatever its method, whose getter runs the same reader and keeps what it read. The guard chooses only whether the read happens here, asynchronously, or there, synchronously, and either way it happens once and for every method
!TryStripSIG0(...) || unsigned is null - the same, for the other kind
unsigned is null || sig is null, that chain one term along. The second || on the line is the type-covered test, and a test kills it

bound.Count < endPoints.Count && !portChosenBySystem, which guards a logger.LogWarning and nothing else. Both mutations of the line change which runs are logged about, and nothing that reaches a socket

the twelve-octet floor of BuildNotAuthorizedResponse. It answers a request whose signature did not verify, so the request carried a TSIG or a SIG(0) and is an order of magnitude longer than the header it is measured against

bound.Count < endPoints.Count && !portChosenBySystem, which guards a logger.LogWarning and nothing else. Both mutations of the line change which runs are logged about, and nothing that reaches a socket

signingKeys is null || !SignaturesExpireAt.HasValue. The two are assigned once each, six lines apart in Sign and with no path between them that can fail, so they are null together and set together - and where the two operands always agree, or and and cannot
Name is null || nsec3Parameters is null in MatchingNSEC3. Its three callers pass a name they have already checked, and with no parameters HashOf returns null on the next line anyway

end < 0 ? null : response[..end], under FindEndOfQuestions, which sets the stream to offset 12 before it reads a question and returns either its position or -1. Zero is not among its answers, so < 0 and <= 0 agree on every one. The first sweep recorded this line killed by Dnssec, one test of 326, in a pass-2 row that had come back BUILD-FAILED and was measured again by hand; nothing in the line or in the function below it has changed since, and the second sweep finds no project that fails. The kill was the re-measurement's noise

IsHEAD: false on the 'not an HTTP method this server knows' reply. HTTPMethod.TryParse returns null only for a name that violates RFC 9110 section 9.1's token syntax - an unknown but well-formed name becomes a new HTTPMethod - and a :method pseudo-header that breaks the token rules is refused by the client stack before it reaches a socket
the same guard in CoveringNSEC3. Name can be null here - NextCloser returns null when QNAME is the encloser - but HashOf answers null for that too

listener.Client.DualMode = false on the UDP side. Its own comment says why: with the IPv4 listener actually bound, IPv4 datagrams go to the IPv4 socket and the flag is never consulted. It states the intent and guards the degraded case where the second bind is removed
the NSEC3 twin of 306, over hashes
target.IndexOf('?') is var mark && mark >= 0. The two readings differ only for a :path that begins with the question mark, and HTTP/2 origin-form requires it to begin with a slash
the NSEC3 twin of 307

the NSEC3 wrap, and NOT for the reason its NSEC twin at 311 dies. The two readings differ only when owner and next are the same hash, which needs a chain of one record - and every NSEC3 proof that asks for a covering record has already asked for a matching one, which in such a zone is that same record. Collect drops the duplicate, so the response is identical whichever way the comparison reads. The NSEC branch has no matching call to fall back on, which is why the same mutation is a gap there and not here
label is null || label.Length == 0 in OwnerHashOf. Split always yields at least one element, so FirstOrDefault over it is never null and only the length test can fire
IsHEAD: false on the 500. Reaching it needs the handler to throw, which a well-formed request cannot arrange from outside
Left[i] < Right[i] ? -1 : 1, under an if that has already established Left[i] != Right[i]. Less-than and less-or-equal cannot disagree where equality is excluded
the bound of ClosestEncloser's walk. Stopping one candidate short loses exactly the apex, and the return below the loop is the apex
qnameLabels.Length <= encloserLabels.Length in NextCloser. The closest provable encloser is an ancestor of QNAME and never QNAME itself, because a name with a matching NSEC3 is a name that exists
soa.Minimum < soa.TimeToLive ? soa.Minimum : soa.TimeToLive. Where the two are equal the branches return the same number, which is the only case the comparison could be changed about
Skip >= Labels.Length ? "." : String.Join('.', Labels.Skip(Skip)) + ".". At equality the other branch joins nothing and appends the dot, which is the same dot the first branch returns
return Records.Length > 0 in TryGetRecords. Add never creates an empty list, and Remove drops the key as soon as its list empties, so a TryGetValue that succeeded has found records
the same flag on the TCP side, for the same reason

length > sharedBuffer.Length, guarding the framed TCP read. The buffer comes from ArrayPool.Shared.Rent(UInt16.MaxValue), which allocates at least that much and in practice the next power of two, while length is a UInt16 and cannot exceed 65535. The comparison is never true, and the mutant is true only where the buffer is exactly 65535 - a size the shared pool's buckets do not produce. A guard that cannot fire either way
